title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: a 4-element set I, the Klein group V(I) of double transpositions of I (the normal Klein subgroup of S_I), and J = J(I), the 3-element set of partitions of I into two pairs. J is identified with V(I)^* = V(I) minus the identity. Earlier pages build an 'octahedral' structure on P^1 with an effective V-action. The 6 fixed points S of V come in 3 pairs S^σ, one for each σ in V^*. Each σ swaps the two pairs S^{σ'} and S^{σ''}. The quotient X/V is a P^1 with 3 branch points indexed by J; this is the space called Σ(J). Off S, V acts freely. So an orbit I of V on X minus S is a V-torsor, and its image is a point ζ of Σ(J)^* = Σ(J) minus J. There is a canonical model X(I) built from I, with V(I) acting on it and X(I)/V(I) ≅ Σ(J).

On this page:
(1) Given an effective action V = V(I) on X, one gets a V-torsor I(V) from the octahedron Oc(V,X), and a canonical isomorphism X ≅ X(I(V)).
(2) Twisting is compatible with this: X(T ∧ T') = X(T) ∧_V T' for V-torsors T, T'. He notes this is still to be made explicit ('expliciter').
(3) Put t = δ(I,X) := I(V) ∧ I^{-1}, the difference torsor (V is abelian). Then X ≅ X(I) ∧_V t, and X/V ≅ X(I)/V ≅ Σ(J).
(4) Proposition: for fixed I (hence J and V = V(J)), giving a P^1 X with an embedding V ↪ Aut(X) is equivalent to giving a V-torsor t, via t ↦ X(I) ∧_V t.
(5) Hence giving (X, I ↪ X) is equivalent to giving (a) a point ζ of Σ(J)^* and (b) a V-torsor t together with a V-isomorphism X_ζ = X(I)_ζ ∧ t ≅ I. In other words t = I ∧ X(I)_ζ^{-1}, so the data reduce to ζ alone.

The next page states the result as a theorem over an algebraically closed k of characteristic ≠ 2. The groupoid of projective lines with 4 marked points labelled by I is equivalent to the groupoid of pairs (I, ξ ∈ Σ(J(I))^*).

In modern terms this is a canonical, coordinate-free and S_4-equivariant identification M_{0,I} ≅ Σ(J(I))^* ≅ P^1 minus 3 points. S_4 acts through S_4 → S_3 = Aut(J). The identification is presented as twisting a universal V-equivariant P^1 by V-torsors. Classically this is the λ-line, or cross-ratio, together with the fact that every double transposition of 4 points on P^1 is induced by a unique involution. The project, 'Chirurgie des surfaces conformes', uses it as a building block: the 4-pointed sphere and its canonical dessin.
errors: No mathematical error. The torsor bookkeeping (difference torsor, the twisting formula, t = I ∧ X(I)_ζ^{-1}) is consistent.
Gap: the formula X(T∧T') = X(T)∧_V T' is asserted but left to be made explicit.
Gap: the construction of X(I) itself is only alluded to (it is on earlier pages).

ideas.what: Every double transposition of 4 distinct points on P^1 is induced by a unique involution. This gives a canonical faithful action of the Klein group V(I) on any 4-pointed P^1, with octahedral fixed-point structure (6 points in 3 pairs).
ideas.modern_name: Klein four-group action on 4-pointed P^1; octahedral configuration

ideas.what: Quotient P^1/V ≅ P^1 with 3 branch points indexed by J. The image of I gives a canonical, S_4-equivariant isomorphism M_{0,I} ≅ Σ(J)^* (P^1 minus 3 points).
ideas.modern_name: M_{0,4} ≅ P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, λ-line / cross-ratio, S_4 → S_3
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Klein); modern moduli formulation folklore
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and the Teichmüller tower but not this torsor formulation

ideas.what: Description of all 4-pointed lines as twists X(I) ∧_V t of a universal model by V-torsors, with t determined by the fibre over ζ: t = I ∧ X(I)_ζ^{-1}.
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by torsors / description of the Klein-group cover of M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard descent and twisting technique (Grothendieck, Serre)

missed.claim: The torsor formulation is natural over an arbitrary base, where V-torsors and forms of P^1 need not be trivial. Grothendieck states it only over an algebraically closed field. Over a general base it would describe 4-pointed conics and give a stack-level, functorial description of M_{0,4}. This is a minor, essentially known point.
missed.quote: la donnée d'un X et d'un plongement V ↪ G_X équivaut à la donnée d'un torseur t sous V, via δ ⟼ X(I) ∧_V t
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal: a clean, canonical (S_4-equivariant) model of M_{0,4} and its V-cover. This is useful for Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type canonical constructions, but known in substance.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, canonical, torsor-theoretic rewriting of the classical identification of 4-pointed P^1's with points of P^1 minus 3 points via the Klein four-group. It is neat Grothendieck-style bookkeeping, but the mathematics is classical.
transcription_corrections: 'au-dessus de α(V)' should read 'au-dessus de Oc(V)' (the octahedron), or similar.
'Ẋ(J)' in the boxed formula and in the Prop is Σ(J) in the image, consistent with the next page.
Inserted line reads 'une opération de V sur X'.
The torsor is first written δ, then renamed t: 't = δ(I,X)'.
'Théo : Prop' is a heading 'Prop.' with 'Théo' crossed or overwritten.
The final struck line is 'X_ζ = fibre de ...'; the kept formula is X_ζ = X(I)_ζ ∧ t ≃ I, i.e. t = I ∧ X(I)_ζ^{-1}.
